## P2 Major

### UX-006 — Make "Done & next" reversible and say what was done
- **Status:** Improved (first seen 2026-11-01). The queue's "✓ Done" names the task and offers Undo. "Done & next" and "Done with a follow-up" still don't.
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager moving through focus mode.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/tasks/actions.ts:44` redirects to `/tasks/next?msg=Done. Here's your next task.` with no `undo`. `tasks/next/route.ts` passes on only `msg`. `actions.ts:45` handles the follow-up case without `undo`.
- **What the user experiences:** After "Done & next →" the bar reads "Done. Here's your next task.", with no task name and no way back. That is the fastest path in the app, and the finished task is already off screen.
- **Why it matters:** A slip in focus mode costs more than a slip in the queue.
- **Recommendation:** Pass `undo={id}` through `/tasks/next` so `TaskFlash` shows `Completed "Issue certificate for Bluefin Analytics". Undo`. Add Undo to "Done — follow-up set for Nov 12" too, and cancel that follow-up when Undo is used.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  ┌ Done. Here's your next task. ──────────────────┐
  AFTER   ┌ Completed "Issue certificate for Bluefin        ◀
          │  Analytics".                          [Undo]    ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-006.html` (earlier run, still accurate)
- **Verify:** Click "Done & next", then Undo on the next task's page. The first task returns at the same rank.

### UX-009 — Keep typed values on the last two forms that lose them
- **Status:** Improved (first seen 2026-11-01). The client, certificate, endorsement, policy and opportunity forms keep what was typed. Receipt and cancellation still don't.
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Accounting manager recording a payment; account manager recording a cancellation.
- **Where:** `accounting/actions.ts:15-17,24` (`guard` redirects with only `?client=`); `policies/actions.ts:133` (cancel redirects with only `error`).
- **What the user experiences:** A receipt refused for a locked month comes back with the amount, check number and memo empty. A cancellation refused for its date comes back with today's date, the first reason and the default return premium.
- **Why it matters:** These are the two forms where retyping invites a money or date error.
- **Recommendation:** Move both forms to the `useActionState` and `rejected()` pattern that `EndorseForm` already uses.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  ✖ That period is locked.
          Amount [        ]  Check # [      ]  Memo [      ]
  AFTER   ✖ That period is locked.
          Amount [2500.00]  Check # [10442]  Memo [Oct renewal]  ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** Post a receipt dated in a locked month. The typed values remain.

### UX-037 — Load the client's details the moment it is picked
- **Status:** Improved (first seen 2026-11-02). Saving against the wrong client is blocked, but the normal path still fails first.
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager logging a call from "＋ New → Task"; accounting manager recording a payment.
- **Where:** `components/client-picker.tsx:11,95`; `tasks/new/page.tsx:27-30`; `accounting/receipts/new/page.tsx:34`.
- **What the user experiences:** The user picks "Brown Electric", types a subject and clicks Create task. The browser refuses: "This form is still for another client. Press the Load button by the client box first." Load "clears anything you typed below".
- **Why it matters:** It costs one failed submit and the typed text on a frequent path.
- **Recommendation:** Submit the picker's GET form when a client is picked and remove the Load buttons. On New task, put the client first and show the other fields once it resolves.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Client [Brown Electric] [Load policies]
          Subject [Call back re: new truck]  [Create task]
          → "This form is still for another client…"          ◀
  AFTER   Client [Brown Electric ▾]  (policies load on pick)  ◀
          Policy [BEA-1123 · Commercial auto ▾]               ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-037.html` (earlier run, direction still right)
- **Verify:** Pick a client and create a task with no extra click.

### UX-040 — Start a reissue from the old certificate, and stop pre-ticking Additional insured
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** CSR changing a certificate while the client waits on the phone.
- **Where:** `certificates/[id]/page.tsx:44` ("Reissue with changes" passes only `client` and `holder`); `certificates/new/page.tsx:43` (`ai: wantsAI || !task`).
- **What the user experiences:** A certificate has Additional insured, Waiver and Primary & non-contributory on GL and Umbrella. "Reissue with changes" opens with only Additional insured ticked and every liability policy ticked. Any certificate started outside a task prints additional insured wording by default.
- **Why it matters:** Issuing replaces the old certificate, so a waiver dropped by accident reaches the holder as a coverage statement.
- **Recommendation:** Add `from={id}` and load the wording, policies and description from that certificate, with the banner "Starting from COI-26-01190. Change what differs." When there is no source certificate, default all three boxes off.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  [x] Additional insured  [ ] Waiver  [ ] Primary & NC   ◀
          [x] GL  [x] Auto  [x] WC  [x] Umbrella                 ◀
  AFTER   Starting from COI-26-01190. Change what differs.       ◀
          [x] Additional insured  [x] Waiver  [x] Primary & NC
          [x] GL  [ ] Auto  [ ] WC  [x] Umbrella
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-040.html`
- **Verify:** Reissue a certificate that has all three flags. The form opens matching it.

### UX-041 — Update the email and description when the holder changes
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** CSR issuing to a holder other than the one preselected.
- **Where:** `certificates/new/page.tsx:41-42` computes `email` and `description` once; `holder-choice.tsx:20` changes only the "replaces" note; `issue-form.tsx:41` and `holder-choice.tsx:30` both show a holder email field.
- **What the user experiences:** The CSR switches from Hendrick Brothers to Crescent Realty. "Email to" and the description of operations still belong to Hendrick.
- **Why it matters:** A certificate can go to the wrong third party, or describe the wrong job.
- **Recommendation:** Pass each holder's email and last description to the form. On change, replace them unless the user has edited them; if they have, offer "Use Crescent's: leasing@crescentrealty.com". Use one Delivery email field in new-holder mode.

  ```

          Email to [pm@hendrickbros.com]          (Hendrick's)  ◀
  AFTER   Holder [Crescent Realty Partners ▾]
          Email to [leasing@crescentrealty.com]                 ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** Change the holder. Email and description follow it unless already edited.

### UX-044 — Keep coverage-risk work from leaving the queue past its deadline
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** M
- **Who / when:** Account manager clearing "Do now" between interruptions.
- **Where:** `components/tasks.tsx:39-48` ("✓ Done" and "Next week" on every row); `lib/priority.ts:101` (a snoozed task stays out until its date); `lib/work.ts:215-226` (the daily non-pay reminder raises priority but keeps the snooze).
- **What the user experiences:** On "cancels Nov 12 unless paid", "Next week" is one click away and hides the task past the cancellation. "✓ Done" closes it with no outcome.
- **Why it matters:** Coverage can lapse with nobody looking, on the very items the queue ranks highest.
- **Recommendation:** For `NONPAY`, `UW-CANC`, `BINDER-EXP` and renewals within 7 days:
  - Replace "✓ Done" with "Resolve →".
  - Disable any snooze past the deadline and label it "after Nov 12".
  - Clear the snooze 2 days before the deadline.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Piedmont Haulers … cancels 2026-11-12   [✓ Done] [⏱ Later]
          Snooze until: [Tomorrow] [3 days] [Next week]
  AFTER   Piedmont Haulers … cancels Nov 12      [Resolve →] [⏱ Later] ◀
          Snooze until: [Tomorrow] [3 days] · Next week: after Nov 12  ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-044.html`
- **Verify:** A non-pay task can't be snoozed past its cancel date.

### UX-020 — Finish field names and lift the remaining faint text
- **Status:** Improved (first seen 2026-11-01)
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Keyboard and screen-reader users; anyone in bright light.
- **Where:**
  - `ClientPicker` is announced as "Client" where its label says "Insured" or "Client with an open balance": `certificates/new/page.tsx:16`, `claims/new/page.tsx:16`, `accounting/receipts/new/page.tsx:34`.

### UX-048 — Offer a way back from Ignored, Cancelled and Lost
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager who ignored an email by mistake; producer whose lost deal revives.

  ```
  AFTER   Trust cash                         $84,210.00       ◀
          less Carriers and wholesalers     −$61,002.11       ◀
          Excess available to sweep          $22,181.45       ◀
  ```
- **Verify:** The rows add up to the excess.

### UX-054 — Connect endorsement, invoice and receipt
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** M
- **Who / when:** CSR answering "what did my check pay?"; account manager billing an endorsement.
- **Where:** `policies/actions.ts:83` (the flash names no invoice); `policies/[id]/page.tsx:145-154`; `clients/[id]/page.tsx:376-390` (invoice numbers aren't links, and receipts don't show what they paid).
- **What the user experiences:** "Endorsement issued" never mentions the invoice it created, and a receipt doesn't show which invoices it paid.
- **Why it matters:** An invoice nobody knows about doesn't get sent.
- **Recommendation:** Flash "Endorsement issued. Invoice INV-26-0433 for $412.00 created. [Open PDF]". Show "Paid by RCT-…" under each invoice and "Applied to …" under each receipt.
- **Verify:** From a policy transaction, reach its invoice and the receipt that paid it.

### UX-055 — Show term and status in the claim's policy list
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager recording a loss.
- **Where:** `claims/new/page.tsx:18,25,29`.
- **What the user experiences:** Expired and cancelled terms appear as "GRM-GL-5512-02 · General liability · Granite Ridge", with no dates or status.
- **Why it matters:** A claim filed against the wrong term goes to the wrong record.
- **Recommendation:** Label each option "… · Jun 8 2026–Jun 8 2027 · in force", and warn when the date of loss is outside the chosen term.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  GRM-GL-5512-02 · General liability · Granite Ridge
  AFTER   GRM-GL-5512-02 · GL · Jun 8 2026–Jun 8 2027 · in force  ◀
  ```
- **Verify:** A date of loss outside the term shows a warning.

### UX-056 — Update the checklist when a task's type changes
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager correcting a misread email.
- **Where:** `inbox/actions.ts:43` updates the code, priority and subject only; `lib/email/ingest.ts:238`.
- **What the user experiences:** After retyping a task to "Certificate request", the checklist and due date still belong to the old type.
- **Why it matters:** The checklist then steers the user through the wrong job.
- **Recommendation:** Replace the checklist if nothing is ticked, otherwise append the new steps. Re-derive the due date, and flash "Now a Certificate request, due Nov 10."
- **Verify:** A retyped task's checklist matches its new type.

### UX-057 — Don't call it "Send reply" when nothing is sent
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager replying while outbound email isn't connected.
- **Where:** `inbox/[id]/page.tsx:54`; `inbox/actions.ts:107-110`.
- **What the user experiences:** The button says "Send reply". The task note reads "Reply to …" with an "email" pill, and the Replies tab lists it like a sent message.
- **Why it matters:** Anyone checking later would believe the client got the reply.
- **Recommendation:** With SMTP off, label the button "Log reply (not sent)", store the note as "Not sent: reply drafted for …", and mark it in Replies.
- **Verify:** With SMTP unset, no record suggests a reply went out.

### UX-058 — Mark required fields
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03)
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Everyone, especially on rarely used forms.
- **Where:** `components/ui.tsx:162` (`Field` has no required state).
- **What the user experiences:** Required and optional fields look the same until the browser stops the save.
- **Why it matters:** A marker saves a failed submit on long forms.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `required` prop to `Field` that renders a small "Required" tag next to the label.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Carrier [Choose… ▾]
  AFTER   Carrier · Required [Choose… ▾]     ◀
  ```
- **Verify:** Every `required` input shows the marker.

### UX-059 — Bring the queue up on a phone and mark the current page
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-11-03). It got worse this run: the AI box (UX-064) now sits above the six tiles.
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Producer or account manager on a phone.
- **Where:** `page.tsx:107-109`; `components/shell.tsx:52-54` (no active state, `text-xs` links); `components/tasks.tsx:39-48`.
- **What the user experiences:** The phone shows the greeting, the AI box, suggestion chips and three rows of tiles before the first task. "✓ Done" is a small target.
- **Why it matters:** The queue is the point of the screen.
- **Recommendation:** Below `sm`, show one strip, "Overdue 4 · Today 7 · Email 3". Add `aria-current` and active styling to `MobileNav`. Give the quick actions a 40px-high row of their own.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  [Ask the AI…][Ask] / chips / 6 tiles / Priority queue
  AFTER   Overdue 4 · Today 7 · Email 3                      ◀
          Priority queue …   [✓ Done] [⏱ Later] (40px)       ◀
  ```
- **Verify:** At 375px the first task shows without scrolling.

### UX-064 — Put the AI box below the queue, and hide it when it can't be used
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager opening My Day; CSR on a busy morning; anyone on a phone.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/page.tsx:107` places `AskBox` between the header and the stats. `components/ask-box.tsx:17-21` still renders a disabled input with the note "The AI Assistant isn't available right now." The client page "Ask about this account" box does the same (`clients/[id]/page.tsx:112-117`).
- **What the user experiences:** The first thing under "Good morning, Marisol" is a full-width box with three suggestion chips. One of them, "What should I work on next?", duplicates the "Start next task" button right above it. Where no API key is set, the box is greyed out but still takes the top slot, with a sentence explaining it doesn't work. The queue starts lower on every screen.
- **Why it matters:** My Day exists to answer "what next?" at a glance. A permanently dead control in the prime spot pushes the ranked answer down and invites a second, slower route to the same answer.
- **Recommendation:**
  - Move the box into the right column as a compact "Ask about your work" card under "Email to triage", or into the header next to search.
  - Drop the "What should I work on next?" chip from My Day; keep "What's at risk this week?".
  - When the assistant is off, don't render the box at all on My Day or the client page. The Assistant page itself can keep explaining why it is unavailable.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Good morning, Marisol          [＋ Task] [Start next task →]
          [Ask the AI Assistant anything          ] [Ask]      ◀
          (What should I work on next?) (What's at risk…)      ◀
          [Overdue][Due today][Emails][Chase][Renewals][Done]
  AFTER   Good morning, Marisol          [＋ Task] [Start next task →]
          [Overdue][Due today][Emails][Chase][Renewals][Done]
          Priority queue …          │ Email to triage …
                                    │ Ask about your work [    ][Ask] ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-064.html`
- **Verify:** With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset, My Day shows no AI box. With it set, the first task row sits higher than it does today.

### UX-065 — Make client documents read like documents
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Client paying an invoice; a driver showing an ID card at a traffic stop; a certificate holder checking the issue date. These are the people who receive the documents.
- **Where:** `web/src/lib/pdf.ts`:
  - `:208`: invoice header "Issued 2026-11-03 · due 2026-12-03 · OPEN".
  - `:211-215`: amounts drawn left-aligned at x=480.
  - `:189`: ID card "Effective 2026-06-08  Expires 2027-06-08".
  - `:121`: certificate "issued 2026-11-03", while its coverage table uses 06/08/2026.
  - `:61`: `row()` cuts every cell at 80 characters with no ellipsis, which affects dec page coverages, interests and invoice lines.
- **What the user experiences:** The invoice shows an internal status word ("OPEN", "PARTIAL") where a client looks for what to pay and by when. "$1,250.00" and "$85.00" don't line up, so Total, Paid and Balance due are hard to compare. ID cards and headers use year-first dates that US readers and police don't expect. A long coverage or mortgagee name is cut off mid-word.
- **Why it matters:** A document is the agency's face to people outside it. Misaligned totals and odd dates make a client call to ask, and a truncated interest name can look like an error to a lender.
- **Recommendation:**
  - Use `MM/DD/YYYY` (the existing `shortDate`) for every date on every PDF.
  - Right-align money with a `right` option on `row()`, as `cells()` already does for limits.
  - Replace the status word with "Amount due $1,165.00 by 12/03/2026", "Paid in full" or "Credit $40.00".
  - Wrap long text instead of slicing it.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Invoice INV-26-0433
          Issued 2026-11-03 · due 2026-12-03 · OPEN              ◀
          Endorsement: add 2026 RAV4         $412.00             ◀
          Total                              $1,250.00
  AFTER   Invoice INV-26-0433 · Issued 11/03/2026
          Amount due $1,165.00 by 12/03/2026                     ◀
          Endorsement: add 2026 RAV4             $412.00         ◀
          Total                                $1,250.00         ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-065.html`
- **Verify:** Open an invoice, an ID card and a dec page. Every date is MM/DD/YYYY, money columns line up at the decimal point, and no text ends mid-word.

### UX-066 — After Reassign, name who has it and move on to the next task
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager in focus mode handing a task to a colleague, for example a personal-lines request that belongs to another desk.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/tasks/actions.ts:86-90` returns to the same task with "Reassigned". `tasks/[id]/page.tsx:149-150` then replaces the Finish panel with "This is Priya Shah's task. Ask them, or a principal, to change it."
- **What the user experiences:** After clicking Reassign, the flash says only "Reassigned". The page now tells the user they can't act on a task they owned a second ago, and there is no next step on screen. They must click "Next task →" in the header to continue.
- **Why it matters:** Handing off is part of working the queue. The screen should confirm who has the task now and keep the user moving, as "Done & next" does.
- **Recommendation:** When the user reassigns away from themselves, redirect to `/tasks/next` with the flash "Reassigned 'Add RAV4 to auto' to Priya Shah." Keep the current behaviour for principals reassigning someone else's work. Offer Undo, which reassigns the task back.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  ✔ Reassigned
          Finish this task: This is Priya Shah's task. Ask them…  ◀
  AFTER   ✔ Reassigned "Add RAV4 to auto" to Priya Shah. [Undo]   ◀
          (your next task, in focus mode)                         ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** Reassign your own task from focus mode. You land on your next task with a message naming the new owner.

## P4 Polish

**UX-024 — Format the remaining dates one way.** (Improved, first seen 2026-11-01.) Year-first dates remain in:
- the non-pay panel and pending banner (`policies/[id]/page.tsx:77,131`);
- the policy header and every Term column;
- the claim header ("loss 2026-11-02");
- certificate "Earliest expiration";
- every money table's Due, Paid and Oldest columns;
- automation task subjects.

Use `whenDate` in running text and a short US date in tables. The client-facing PDFs are covered separately in UX-065.

**UX-060 — Make the My Day badge match the header count.** (Open, first seen 2026-11-03.) The sidebar counts tasks due by today (`layout.tsx:20-21`). "N tasks need you today" counts Do now plus Today, and Do now includes urgent tasks due later (`priority.ts:115`). Use one rule for both.

**UX-061 — Say "today", not "0d" or "-5d".** (Open, first seen 2026-11-03.) The raw `{left}d` form remains on the renewals board (`renewals/page.tsx:90`), the policy list "(Nd)" (`policies/page.tsx:63`) and the client overview, where it can go negative (`clients/[id]/page.tsx:105`). Use `daysLeft`, and "expired" for negatives.

**UX-062 — Use one word per thing.** (Open, first seen 2026-11-03.) Examples:
- "Next week" vs "1 week" for the same snooze (`tasks.tsx:48`, `tasks/[id]/page.tsx:181`).
- "Coming later" and "Needs setup" on controls vs "Not in MVP" and "Pending dependency" on the Roadmap.
- "phase 2" on the Sales footer.
- "loaded by ai" on statements.
- A bare "Create" on the opportunity form.

**UX-063 — Hide dead ends; guard the `n` shortcut.** (Open, first seen 2026-11-03.)
- A CSR's Reports page holds a sentence and two "Coming later" tags.
- Admin cards a non-admin can't open are dimmed but still link to a refusal (`admin/page.tsx:24`).
- `n` jumps to the next task from any page with a half-filled form (`shell.tsx:88`).
- The README still says `n` creates a task.

**UX-067 — Take setup variables, catalog IDs and token counts out of staff screens.** (New.) Staff see developer language in several places:
- "set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to turn it on" (`clients/[id]/page.tsx:117`), "AI comparison needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" (`policies/[id]/page.tsx:178`), "needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" (`commissions/page.tsx:64`), the Assistant page's "it needs an Anthropic API key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)", and "(email sending needs SMTP_URL)" in a certificate flash.
- Catalog IDs in card titles: "Policy check (POL-20)", "Commission not received (COM-21)", "(GL-23..25)" on the trust page.
- Every assistant answer ends with "3 rounds · 18,422 tokens (12,001 cached)" (`assistant/chat.tsx:87`).

Say "Not set up yet: ask your administrator" and link to Admin › System status. Drop the IDs from titles, since the Roadmap already holds them. Show token counts only on Admin › AI Assistant use.

## What works well
- **Claim task to claim.** `tasks/[id]/page.tsx:61` offers "Open claim" when the task has a claim. `claims/[id]/page.tsx:31` puts "Not reported to the carrier yet… [Mark reported]" at the top, and marking it closes the report task with "Next task →" (`claims/actions.ts:41-55`). Keep this pattern for other record-backed tasks.
- **Ranked queue with reasons.** `lib/priority.ts` puts coverage risk first and shows its reasons as chips. The focus view shows up to eight reasons plus "Also open on this policy". The assistant's "what next" uses the same `queueFor` ranking, so it can't disagree with the queue.
- **Non-pay panel.** `policies/[id]/page.tsx:75-100` leads with the cancel date and puts "Payment confirmed: reinstate" first. It keeps "Carrier cancelled it" disabled until that date.
- **Statement readiness.** `commissions/[id]/page.tsx:74-79` shows a ✔/✖ checklist and a disabled button that says what's left ("Resolve 7 lines to post").
- **Dead certificates look dead.** The superseded/revoked banner, the "COVERAGE NO LONGER IN FORCE" line on the PDF and the watermark (`pdf.ts:121-123,155`) work together.
- **Honest assistant framing.** `assistant/about/page.tsx` explains in plain words what the assistant can see and what it can't do, lists the lookups per role, and says "Check what matters… Follow the links before acting." Answers can only link inside the app.
